23	At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.
24	
25	At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel.
26	
27	At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, and the verification interval begins when that reduced pilot command has been sent. The verification interval is the period across which the measured branch current must remain above the branch current limit, after the reduced pilot command has been sent, before the ordered shedding step 212 is entered.
28	
29	At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.
30	
31	The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212 while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.

At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel.

At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, and the verification interval begins when that reduced pilot command has been sent. The verification interval is the period across which the measured branch current must remain above the branch current limit, after the reduced pilot command has been sent, before the ordered shedding step 212 is entered.

At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212 while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 supplies the installation and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.

A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. Two connector channels are shown for clarity of illustration. Any number of connector channels of two or more may be connected to the branch conductor 102, and the description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.

A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels and is not affected by a failure, a miswiring or a scaling error in any one connector channel. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.

An edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller, is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, and provides isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels.

FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value under which the edge controller 106 stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel and which the signed local authorization token names when it authorizes that connector channel.

The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.

FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session.

A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, as described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A fault indicator 116 at the installation is coupled to the edge controller 106 and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.

FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.

At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit so that a step in the non-charging load 118 does not by itself carry the branch above its limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.

At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained. Where the available charging current is insufficient to give the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, the edge controller 106 withholds the assignment from one or more connector channels rather than assigning to every connector channel a limit below its minimum sustaining current, and a connector channel from which the assignment is withheld is a connector channel that cannot receive the minimum sustaining current at that allocation interval. In distributing the remainder, a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller.

At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.

At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel.

At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, and the verification interval begins when that reduced pilot command has been sent. The verification interval is the period across which the measured branch current must remain above the branch current limit, after the reduced pilot command has been sent, before the ordered shedding step 212 is entered.

At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212 while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current chosen so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106, retained in the nonvolatile memory 112 so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.

During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its network connection will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.

Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence at the edge controller 106. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. On entry of a commissioning mode through the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time, that is, it drives the control pilot signalling of one commanded connector channel through a transition that is sufficient for the connector channel to be identified by its current sensing but that does not require a charging session to be established, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

1	Parking structures, fleet depots, workplaces and multi unit dwellings commonly install several electric vehicle connectors on a single electrical branch. The conductors, overcurrent device and upstream transformer capacity of that branch are sized for an aggregate current that is lower, and often much lower, than the sum of the individual current ratings of the connectors served by it. The installation therefore depends on a control function that continuously divides the branch capacity among the connectors that are in use, rather than on the physical rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A control function of this kind ordinarily issues a current limit to each vehicle over a control pilot signalling interface. The limit is advisory in the sense that it is a request addressed to equipment that the site operator does not own and cannot inspect. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous current for an interval after a new limit is signalled, or may not follow the signalled limit at all. Auxiliary equipment on the same branch, such as lighting, ventilation, elevators or refrigeration, draws current that the charging control function does not command and that changes without notice. A control function that computes an allocation and then assumes the allocation has taken effect can therefore hold the branch above its rated aggregate current while every connector believes it is compliant, with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection.
4	Site controllers of this class also depend on a network connection to a remote management service for schedules, tariffs and driver authorization. Connectivity in a below grade parking structure or a remote depot is intermittent. A controller that treats loss of connectivity as a reason to stop charging strands vehicles that were already authorized, while a controller that treats loss of connectivity as permission to charge without restraint abandons the branch limit that the last accepted configuration established, and abandons the accounting record that billing depends on.
5	
6	A further difficulty arises at installation. The connector identifier used by the control function, the physical contactor that energizes a connector and the current sensing channel that measures it are joined by field wiring performed once, often by a contractor who does not operate the equipment afterwards. If that wiring map is recorded incorrectly, the control function will deliver a computed current limit to one connector while measuring another. Every subsequent verification appears to succeed, because the two errors are consistent with one another, and the fault is discovered only when the branch overcurrent device operates or when a vehicle receives a limit that was intended for a different vehicle.
7	
8	There remains a need for a controller that treats the aggregate current of the branch as a measured quantity, verified independently of the per connector measurements and independently of any vehicle response, and that converts an unanswered current reduction into a bounded, ordered and recoverable removal of load rather than into an uncontrolled trip of the branch overcurrent device.

Parking structures, fleet depots, workplaces and multi unit dwellings commonly install several electric vehicle connectors on a single electrical branch. The conductors, overcurrent device and upstream transformer capacity of that branch are sized for an aggregate current that is lower, and often much lower, than the sum of the individual current ratings of the connectors served by it. The installation therefore depends on a control function that continuously divides the branch capacity among the connectors that are in use, rather than on the physical rating of any one connector.

A control function of this kind ordinarily issues a current limit to each vehicle over a control pilot signalling interface. The limit is advisory in the sense that it is a request addressed to equipment that the site operator does not own and cannot inspect. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous current for an interval after a new limit is signalled, or may not follow the signalled limit at all. Auxiliary equipment on the same branch, such as lighting, ventilation, elevators or refrigeration, draws current that the charging control function does not command and that changes without notice. A control function that computes an allocation and then assumes the allocation has taken effect can therefore hold the branch above its rated aggregate current while every connector believes it is compliant, with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection.
Site controllers of this class also depend on a network connection to a remote management service for schedules, tariffs and driver authorization. Connectivity in a below grade parking structure or a remote depot is intermittent. A controller that treats loss of connectivity as a reason to stop charging strands vehicles that were already authorized, while a controller that treats loss of connectivity as permission to charge without restraint abandons the branch limit that the last accepted configuration established, and abandons the accounting record that billing depends on.

A further difficulty arises at installation. The connector identifier used by the control function, the physical contactor that energizes a connector and the current sensing channel that measures it are joined by field wiring performed once, often by a contractor who does not operate the equipment afterwards. If that wiring map is recorded incorrectly, the control function will deliver a computed current limit to one connector while measuring another. Every subsequent verification appears to succeed, because the two errors are consistent with one another, and the fault is discovered only when the branch overcurrent device operates or when a vehicle receives a limit that was intended for a different vehicle.

There remains a need for a controller that treats the aggregate current of the branch as a measured quantity, verified independently of the per connector measurements and independently of any vehicle response, and that converts an unanswered current reduction into a bounded, ordered and recoverable removal of load rather than into an uncontrolled trip of the branch overcurrent device.

At each allocation interval the controller subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current, assigns a minimum sustaining current to each active connector channel that can receive it, and distributes the remainder according to stored energy-deficit values. The assigned current limits are sent through the control-pilot interfaces and verified by the connector current sensors. If branch current remains above the limit for a verification interval after a reduced pilot command, the controller opens contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until branch current is below it.

All twelve findings are resolved and the draft files are synchronized.

**Figures**: FIG-2 drops the mating notch, the hinged-bar contact topology and the encircling non-contact ring, uses the generic straddling square-outline sensor convention already used in FIG-1, and routes the control pilot line from the interface to the vehicle connector rather than around it. input.summary: Repaired all twelve review findings: deleted the undisclosed connector-directed reduction claim and its supporting description text, removed the second definition of the reduced pilot command, deleted the interval-configurability and connector-type sentences, removed untraced vehicle-response behaviour, narrowed the withholding claim to the minimum sustaining current, aligned the method preamble with claim 1, and rebuilt FIG-2 and FIG-3 so the briefs assert no undisclosed mating geometry, contact topology, sensing relationship, signalling route, or containment of the fault indicator. Claims renumbered 1-18 with dependencies corrected; drawings brief, description, numeral table and figure files are synchronized.
reasoning: Claim 1 is untouched. Its distinguishing work is done by the pairing of an upstream branch measurement taken ahead of every connector contactor with per-connector verification, and by the requirement that an unanswered reduction ripens, only after a verification interval measured on the branch, into contactor opening one at a time in a stored shedding order. Deleting old claim 2 removed the only limitation that gave the reduced pilot command a second, connector-level trigger, so the independent claims now express one consistent trigger and one consistent addressee.

The deleted claim 2 subject matter was not replaced by a narrower substitute. The disclosure states the verification act and gives no consequence for a failed verification, so any fallback claim in that direction would have had no description to rest on. The ladder retains its real fallbacks: measure-after-each-open, the three-condition reclosure, welded-contactor isolation with the local fault indicator, the sustaining-first withholding rule, deficit-weighted distribution, the isolated local bus, offline authorization with the signed token, tamper-evident meter records, and the commissioning map with store-only-on-agreement.

Claim 5 (formerly 6) had claimed withholding current generally while the description withholds only the minimum sustaining assignment, the remainder still being distributed by energy deficit afterwards. Narrowing the claim to the minimum sustaining current makes claim and description say the same thing in the same words rather than widening the description to rescue the broader claim.

The method preamble now recites vehicle connectors served by the connector channels, matching claim 1, which recites the contactor as connected between the branch and a respective vehicle connector and keeps the connector outside the channel components. Both independent claims and FIG-2 now express that boundary the same way.

The staged-reduction paragraph previously let the reduced pilot command mean either a targeted command or a lower limit computed at the next allocation interval from increased non-charging load. One term with two referents in one section is an antecedent-basis hazard for the claim term. The paragraph now tracks claim 1 exactly: branch current above the limit, reduced pilot command sent, verification interval running from that transmission.

The fault indicator is a drawing and description question, not a claim question: the claim already recites it as an apparatus element alongside the controller. FIG-3 was corrected to the authoritative text by moving the block outside the controller rectangle and connecting it, rather than by editing the claim or numeral table to match what had been drawn.

FIG-2's contactor and connector current sensor now use the same generic straddling square-outline convention FIG-1 already uses for the branch current sensor. This removes the assertions about which terminal the movable member hinges to, where the bus taps the contactor, and whether the sensor encircles the conductor without touching it, none of which the disclosure states, while still giving each part a visible outline and an unambiguous leader target.

FIG-2's second signalling line now runs from the control-pilot interface to the vehicle connector block instead of bypassing it to the vehicle. The disclosure ties the control-pilot interface to the connector and says nothing about the route to the vehicle, so the figure asserts association rather than a bypassing flow path.

FIG-2 exceeded the 2800 character brief limit after the corrections, so a negative touch constraint on the bus line was replaced with a positive routing statement and one numeral note was shortened. No geometry required by the specification was dropped.
prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so the Background carries no citations and none could be added without inventing one.

A branch conductor 102 supplies the installation and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.

The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.

A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. Two connector channels are shown for clarity of illustration. FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.

Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.

The verification interval is the period across which the measured branch current must remain above the branch current limit, after the reduced pilot command has been sent, before the ordered shedding step 212 is entered.

The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.

FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 is the conductor of that electrical branch and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, and a reference below to the electrical branch is a reference to the branch supplied by the branch conductor 102. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.

A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. Two connector channels are shown for clarity of illustration. Any number of connector channels of two or more may be connected to the branch conductor 102, and the description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.

A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels and is not affected by a failure, a miswiring or a scaling error in any one connector channel. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.

An edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller, is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, and provides isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels.

FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value under which the edge controller 106 stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel and which the signed local authorization token names when it authorizes that connector channel.

The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.

FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106 and the local fault indicator 116 that it operates. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session.

A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, as described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A fault indicator 116 at the installation is coupled to the edge controller 106 and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.

FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.

At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit so that a step in the non-charging load 118 does not by itself carry the branch above its limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.

At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained. Where the available charging current is insufficient to give the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, the edge controller 106 withholds the assignment from one or more connector channels rather than assigning to every connector channel a limit below its minimum sustaining current, and a connector channel from which the assignment is withheld is a connector channel that cannot receive the minimum sustaining current at that allocation interval. In distributing the remainder, a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than a connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller.

At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.

At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel.

At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, and the verification interval begins when that reduced pilot command has been sent. The verification interval is the period across which the measured branch current must remain above the branch current limit, after the reduced pilot command has been sent, before the ordered shedding step 212 is entered.

At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212 while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current chosen so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval, where the energy-deficit value accumulated while it was shed gives it a larger share of the remainder of the available charging current.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106, retained in the nonvolatile memory 112 so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.

During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its network connection will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.

Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence at the edge controller 106. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. On entry of a commissioning mode through the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time, that is, it drives the control pilot signalling of one commanded connector channel through a transition that is sufficient for the connector channel to be identified by its current sensing but that does not require a charging session to be established, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

# FIG. 3

A flat block diagram of the edge controller in plain black line work on white, no shading and no text inside the drawing area. All line work stays well inside the drawing area, clear of the filing margins.

One large rectangle occupies the left and central portion of the drawing area and represents the edge controller. Five smaller empty rectangles lie inside it:

- a rectangle at the centre, the processing unit;
- a rectangle to the right of the processing unit at the same height, the session record store;
- a rectangle above the processing unit, the network interface;
- a rectangle below the processing unit, the nonvolatile memory;
- a rectangle to the left of the processing unit at the same height, the service input.

A straight solid line joins the processing unit to each of the other four inner rectangles, running from an edge of the processing unit to the nearest edge of that rectangle. These four lines do not cross one another.

A further empty rectangle stands outside the large rectangle, beyond its right side in the upper right region of the drawing area, and represents the fault indicator. A solid line runs upward from the upper edge of the processing unit, turns right, passes above the session record store rectangle, crosses the right side of the large rectangle and meets the left side of the fault indicator rectangle.

draft/07-drawings.md:5:FIG. 3 is a block diagram of the edge controller of FIG. 1 and of the local fault indicator that the edge controller operates.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:13:FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106 and the local fault indicator 116 that it operates. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value represents the accumulated shortfall of energy delivered to that session.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:15:A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, as described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A local fault indicator 116 at the installation is coupled to the edge controller 106 and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:33:At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current chosen so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the local fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.
draft/06-summary.md:7:In further aspects, a contactor is not reclosed until the connector current sensor of its connector channel reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not restore load simultaneously. A welded-contactor condition is recorded when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, whereupon the controller inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch and operates a local fault indicator.
draft/numerals.md:13:| 116 | local fault indicator |

FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 is the conductor of that electrical branch and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, and a reference below to the electrical branch is a reference to the branch supplied by the branch conductor 102. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.

Updated in `draft/numerals.md` (row 116), `draft/08-detailed-description.md` (FIG. 3 introduction, the controller part listing, and the welded-contactor isolation step), `draft/07-drawings.md` (FIG. 3 entry), and `figures/FIG-3.md` (block description, connection sentence, and numeral note).

input.summary: Fixed both terminology-consistency findings. The description now states that branch conductor 102 is the conductor of the electrical branch and that later references to the electrical branch mean the branch it supplies, giving the claim term a numbered referent. The numbered indicator is renamed local fault indicator 116 throughout the numeral table, the Detailed Description, the Brief Description of the Drawings and the FIG-3 brief, matching claims 4 and 16 and the Summary.
reasoning: The claims express every branch relationship against 'the electrical branch' while the description numbered the same element 'branch conductor 102'. Rather than renaming the claim element or the numeral, which would have rippled through four claims and three figure briefs, I added one linking clause in the first description paragraph. That gives the claim term a numbered referent and an express antecedent for the later bare uses of 'the electrical branch', without changing any recited relationship.

I kept 'branch conductor 102' as the numbered part name because the branch current sensor, the parallel channel connections and the FIG-1 geometry are all described against the conductor itself, and the numeral must attach to a drawable physical part. The linking sentence makes the conductor and the branch one stated referent, so both vocabularies now resolve to the same element.

The indicator was aligned on the claim wording rather than the other way round, because 'local fault indicator' is the inventor's own term in the disclosure. Renaming the numbered part therefore restored source wording and claim-description identity at the same time, and 'at the installation' already carried the locality, so no technical matter moved.

The numeral table row was changed with the part name so that numerals.md, the description, the Brief Description and the FIG-3 brief all carry the identical part name for numeral 116, keeping the one-numeral-one-name invariant intact.

No claim, disclosed embodiment, geometry or relationship was touched. Both changes are naming only, and FIG-3's length after the rename remains within the brief limit, so no rendering constraint had to be traded away.

draft/08-detailed-description.md:29:At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:31:The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212 while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
draft/06-summary.md:5:The branch current sensor serves as an independent safety input. Responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for a verification interval after a reduced pilot command has been sent, the controller opens the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a bounded and predetermined sequence, and only to the extent that the measured branch current shows the removal to be necessary, rather than by operation of the branch overcurrent device.
draft/05-background.md:1:Parking structures, fleet depots, workplaces and multi unit dwellings commonly install several electric vehicle connectors on a single electrical branch. The conductors, overcurrent device and upstream transformer capacity of that branch are sized for an aggregate current that is lower, and often much lower, than the sum of the individual current ratings of the connectors served by it. The installation therefore depends on a control function that continuously divides the branch capacity among the connectors that are in use, rather than on the physical rating of any one connector.
draft/05-background.md:3:A control function of this kind ordinarily issues a current limit to each vehicle over a control pilot signalling interface. The limit is advisory in the sense that it is a request addressed to equipment that the site operator does not own and cannot inspect. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous current for an interval after a new limit is signalled, or may not follow the signalled limit at all. Auxiliary equipment on the same branch, such as lighting, ventilation, elevators or refrigeration, draws current that the charging control function does not command and that changes without notice. A control function that computes an allocation and then assumes the allocation has taken effect can therefore hold the branch above its rated aggregate current while every connector believes it is compliant, with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection.
draft/05-background.md:6:A further difficulty arises at installation. The connector identifier used by the control function, the physical contactor that energizes a connector and the current sensing channel that measures it are joined by field wiring performed once, often by a contractor who does not operate the equipment afterwards. If that wiring map is recorded incorrectly, the control function will deliver a computed current limit to one connector while measuring another. Every subsequent verification appears to succeed, because the two errors are consistent with one another, and the fault is discovered only when the branch overcurrent device operates or when a vehicle receives a limit that was intended for a different vehicle.
draft/05-background.md:8:There remains a need for a controller that treats the aggregate current of the branch as a measured quantity, verified independently of the per connector measurements and independently of any vehicle response, and that converts an unanswered current reduction into a bounded, ordered and recoverable removal of load rather than into an uncontrolled trip of the branch overcurrent device.
---CLAIMS---
1:1. An apparatus for controlling charging of electric vehicles at a plurality of vehicle connectors supplied by a common electrical branch having a branch current limit that is lower than a sum of current ratings of the vehicle connectors, the apparatus comprising:
19:2. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to measure the branch current with the branch current sensor after each opening of one of the contactors in the stored shedding order, and to open no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
21:3. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to withhold reclosure of the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until the connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired.
23:4. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a local fault indicator, wherein the controller is further configured to record a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, and, responsive to the recorded welded-contactor condition, to inhibit the contactors of the other connector channels of the plurality of connector channels and to operate the local fault indicator.
25:5. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured, when the available charging current is insufficient to assign the minimum sustaining current to every active connector channel, to withhold assignment of the minimum sustaining current from at least one active connector channel rather than to assign to every active connector channel a limit below the minimum sustaining current of that active connector channel.
27:6. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to distribute the remainder of the available charging current such that an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is larger receives a larger share of the remainder than an active connector channel whose stored energy-deficit value is smaller.
29:7. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising an isolated local bus coupling the controller to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels and to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels, the isolated local bus providing isolation between the controller and circuits of the connector channels.
31:8. The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a network interface and a nonvolatile memory, wherein the controller is configured to receive remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface, to hold a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in the nonvolatile memory, and, during an outage of the network interface, to continue charging sessions that are already authorized subject to the last accepted branch limit and subject to opening the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in the stored shedding order responsive to the measured branch current.
33:9. draft/08-detailed-description.md:29:At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary, and by the edge controller 106 rather than by the branch overcurrent device. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:31:The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal an overcurrent from the branch current sensor 104, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212 while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
draft/06-summary.md:5:The branch current sensor serves as an independent safety input. Responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for a verification interval after a reduced pilot command has been sent, the controller opens the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a bounded and predetermined sequence, and only to the extent that the measured branch current shows the removal to be necessary, rather than by operation of the branch overcurrent device.
draft/05-background.md:1:Parking structures, fleet depots, workplaces and multi unit dwellings commonly install several electric vehicle connectors on a single electrical branch. The conductors, overcurrent device and upstream transformer capacity of that branch are sized for an aggregate current that is lower, and often much lower, than the sum of the individual current ratings of the connectors served by it. The installation therefore depends on a control function that continuously divides the branch capacity among the connectors that are in use, rather than on the physical rating of any one connector.
draft/05-background.md:3:A control function of this kind ordinarily issues a current limit to each vehicle over a control pilot signalling interface. The limit is advisory in the sense that it is a request addressed to equipment that the site operator does not own and cannot inspect. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous current for an interval after a new limit is signalled, or may not follow the signalled limit at all. Auxiliary equipment on the same branch, such as lighting, ventilation, elevators or refrigeration, draws current that the charging control function does not command and that changes without notice. A control function that computes an allocation and then assumes the allocation has taken effect can therefore hold the branch above its rated aggregate current while every connector believes it is compliant, with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection.
draft/05-background.md:6:A further difficulty arises at installation. The connector identifier used by the control function, the physical contactor that energizes a connector and the current sensing channel that measures it are joined by field wiring performed once, often by a contractor who does not operate the equipment afterwards. If that wiring map is recorded incorrectly, the control function will deliver a computed current limit to one connector while measuring another. Every subsequent verification appears to succeed, because the two errors are consistent with one another, and the fault is discovered only when the branch overcurrent device operates or when a vehicle receives a limit that was intended for a different vehicle.
draft/05-background.md:8:There remains a need for a controller that treats the aggregate current of the branch as a measured quantity, verified independently of the per connector measurements and independently of any vehicle response, and that converts an unanswered current reduction into a bounded, ordered and recoverable removal of load rather than into an uncontrolled trip of the branch overcurrent device.
