Responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for a verification interval after a reduced pilot command has been sent, the controller opens the contactors of the plurality of connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a bounded and predetermined sequence, and only to the extent that the measured branch current shows the removal to be necessary.

In further aspects, a contactor is not reclosed until the connector current sensor of its connector channel reports zero connector current, the control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, and a randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not restore load simultaneously. A welded-contactor condition is recorded when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, whereupon the controller inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch and operates a local fault indicator.

In further aspects, the controller receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through a network interface while holding a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory. During a network outage the controller continues already authorized charging sessions subject to the last accepted branch limit and subject to the branch current sensing described above, and does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and has not expired. Meter records are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence and uploaded when communication returns.

In a further aspect, a service input permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors by commanding one low-energy pilot transition at a time and confirming the connector current sensor that responds, the association being stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel, so that a field wiring error cannot cause an assigned current limit to be applied to the wrong vehicle connector.

Corresponding methods are also disclosed.

1	Parking structures, fleet depots, workplaces and multi unit dwellings commonly install several electric vehicle connectors on a single electrical branch. The conductors, overcurrent device and upstream transformer capacity of that branch are sized for an aggregate current that is lower, and often much lower, than the sum of the individual current ratings of the connectors served by it. The installation therefore depends on a control function that continuously divides the branch capacity among the connectors that are in use, rather than on the physical rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A control function of this kind ordinarily issues a current limit to each vehicle over a control pilot signalling interface. The limit is advisory in the sense that it is a request addressed to equipment that the site operator does not own and cannot inspect. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous current for an interval after a new limit is signalled, or may not follow the signalled limit at all. Auxiliary equipment on the same branch, such as lighting, ventilation, elevators or refrigeration, draws current that the charging control function does not command and that changes without notice. A control function that computes an allocation and then assumes the allocation has taken effect can therefore hold the branch above its rated aggregate current while every connector believes it is compliant, with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection.
4	Site controllers of this class also depend on a network connection to a remote management service for schedules, tariffs and driver authorization. Connectivity in a below grade parking structure or a remote depot is intermittent. A controller that treats loss of connectivity as a reason to stop charging strands vehicles that were already authorized, while a controller that treats loss of connectivity as permission to charge without restraint abandons the branch limit that the last accepted configuration established, and abandons the accounting record that billing depends on.
5	
6	A further difficulty arises at installation. The connector identifier used by the control function, the physical contactor that energizes a connector and the current sensing channel that measures it are joined by field wiring performed once, often by a contractor who does not operate the equipment afterwards. If that wiring map is recorded incorrectly, the control function will deliver a computed current limit to one connector while measuring another. Every subsequent verification appears to succeed, because the two errors are consistent with one another, and the fault is discovered only when the branch overcurrent device operates or when a vehicle receives a limit that was intended for a different vehicle.
7	
8	There remains a need for a controller that treats the aggregate current of the branch as a measured quantity, verified independently of the per connector measurements and independently of any vehicle response, and that converts an unanswered current reduction into a bounded, ordered and recoverable removal of load rather than into an uncontrolled trip of the branch overcurrent device.

FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 is the conductor of that electrical branch and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, and a reference below to the electrical branch is a reference to the branch supplied by the branch conductor 102. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.

A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. Two connector channels are shown for clarity of illustration. Any number of connector channels of two or more may be connected to the branch conductor 102, and the description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.

A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels and is not affected by a failure, a miswiring or a scaling error in any one connector channel. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.

An edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller, is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, and provides isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels.

FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value under which the edge controller 106 stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel and which the signed local authorization token names when it authorizes that connector channel.

The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.

FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106 and the local fault indicator 116 that it operates. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value is a value stored for the session and used in distributing the remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels.

A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, as described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A local fault indicator 116 at the installation is coupled to the edge controller 106 and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.

FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.

At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit so that a step in the non-charging load 118 does not by itself carry the branch above its limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.

At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained.

At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.

At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel.

At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, and the verification interval begins when that reduced pilot command has been sent. The verification interval is the period across which the measured branch current must remain above the branch current limit, after the reduced pilot command has been sent, before the ordered shedding step 212 is entered.

At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal from the branch current sensor 104 a measured branch current above the branch current limit, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212 while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current chosen so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the local fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106, retained in the nonvolatile memory 112 so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.

During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its network connection will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.

Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence at the edge controller 106. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. On entry of a commissioning mode through the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time, that is, it drives the control pilot signalling of one commanded connector channel through a transition that is sufficient for the connector channel to be identified by its current sensing but that does not require a charging session to be established, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 is the conductor of that electrical branch and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, and a reference below to the electrical branch is a reference to the branch supplied by the branch conductor 102. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.

A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. The description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel connected to the branch conductor 102, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.

A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.

An edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller, is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, and provides isolation between the edge controller 106 and the circuits of the connector channels.

FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which is the value under which the edge controller 106 stores the state of the charging session at that connector channel and which the signed local authorization token names when it authorizes that connector channel.

The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.

FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106 and the local fault indicator 116 that it operates. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value is a value stored for the session and used in distributing the remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels.

A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, as described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A local fault indicator 116 at the installation is coupled to the edge controller 106 and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.

FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.

At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit so that a step in the non-charging load 118 does not by itself carry the branch above its limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.

At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained.

At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.

At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel.

At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, and the verification interval begins when that reduced pilot command has been sent. The verification interval is the period across which the measured branch current must remain above the branch current limit, after the reduced pilot command has been sent, before the ordered shedding step 212 is entered.

At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal from the branch current sensor 104 a measured branch current above the branch current limit, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212 while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current chosen so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the local fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106, retained in the nonvolatile memory 112 so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.

During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its network connection will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.

Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence at the edge controller 106. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. On entry of a commissioning mode through the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time, that is, it drives the control pilot signalling of one commanded connector channel through a transition that is sufficient for the connector channel to be identified by its current sensing but that does not require a charging session to be established, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands, the pilot reports and the connector current sensor reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels.

The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which the signed local authorization token names when it authorizes that connector channel.

The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current the session would take if the branch had spare capacity. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value is a value stored for the session and used in distributing the remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels.

A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A local fault indicator 116 at the installation is coupled to the edge controller 106 and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.

FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.

At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the actual spare capacity of the branch, and the reserve does not have to be enlarged to cover the worst case of an unmeasured load.

At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel.

The verification interval is the period across which the measured branch current must remain above the branch current limit, after the reduced pilot command has been sent, before the ordered shedding step 212 is entered.

At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A connector channel whose current sensing has failed low, or whose sensing has been crossed with that of another connector channel by a wiring error, cannot conceal from the branch current sensor 104 a measured branch current above the branch current limit, and cannot cause a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212 while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

The leakage threshold is a stored current chosen so that a genuinely open contactor is not reported as welded. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, and the verification interval begins when that reduced pilot command has been sent. The verification interval is the period across which the measured branch current must remain above the branch current limit, after the reduced pilot command has been sent, before the ordered shedding step 212 is entered.

At an ordered shedding step 212, and responsive to the measured branch current remaining above the branch current limit for the verification interval after the reduced pilot command has been sent, the edge controller 106 opens the contactors of the connector channels one at a time in a stored shedding order until the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. The stored shedding order lists the connector channels of the branch in the sequence in which they are to be removed. After each contactor is opened, the edge controller 106 reads the branch current sensor 104 again, and it opens no further contactor once the measured branch current is below the branch current limit. Load is therefore removed in a known sequence, in the smallest number of steps that the measured branch current shows to be necessary. Ordered shedding under measurement removes as few connector channels as the measurement requires, in the stored shedding order, with the remaining connector channels still charging.

The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A measured branch current above the branch current limit therefore causes a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212 whatever the connector current sensors report, and no contactor is opened at that step while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.

At a welded-contactor isolation step 214, the edge controller 106 records a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel. The leakage threshold is a stored current value. On recording the welded-contactor condition, the edge controller 106 inhibits the contactors of the other connector channels on the electrical branch, so that no further connector channel is closed onto a branch that already carries an uncontrollable load, and operates the local fault indicator 116 at the installation, so that the condition is signalled where the equipment stands. While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed.

At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch, the edge controller 106 does not reclose the contactor of a connector channel that has been opened until three conditions are satisfied together. The connector current sensor of that connector channel reports zero connector current, which confirms that the contactor did in fact open and distinguishes a successfully shed connector channel from a welded one. The control-pilot interface of that connector channel reports a connected vehicle, so that a contactor is not closed onto a connector with no vehicle at it. A randomized recovery delay has expired, so that connector channels that were shed together do not reclose together and return the branch immediately to the condition that caused the shedding. Once the three conditions are satisfied, the contactor is reclosed and the connector channel takes part in the allocation at the next allocation interval.

The edge controller 106 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations through the network interface 110 and applies them to the sessions at the connector channels. It also holds, in the nonvolatile memory 112, a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit. The signed local authorization token names the local connector identifiers it authorizes and carries an expiry. The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106, retained in the nonvolatile memory 112 so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against.

During a network outage the edge controller 106 continues charging sessions that are already authorized, subject to the last accepted branch limit held in the nonvolatile memory 112 and subject to the measurement of the branch current sensor 104 and the staged reduction, ordered shedding, welded-contactor isolation and conditional reclosure described above. The protective process therefore does not depend on the network at any point. The edge controller 106 does not start a charging session at a newly connected vehicle connector during the outage unless the signed local authorization token authorizes the local connector identifier of that connector channel and the token has not expired. An outage thus preserves service for vehicles that were already charging without turning the installation into an unauthorized supply, and the expiry of the token bounds how long an installation that has lost its network connection will keep admitting new sessions on the strength of an old authorization.

Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence at the edge controller 106. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. On entry of a commissioning mode through the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time, that is, it drives the control pilot signalling of one commanded connector channel through a transition that is sufficient for the connector channel to be identified by its current sensing but that does not require a charging session to be established, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. The description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel connected to the branch conductor 102, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.
A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.
An edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller, is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands, the pilot reports and the connector current sensor reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels.
FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which the signed local authorization token names when it authorizes that connector channel.
The two current measurements do different work, and the combination of them is what allows the reduction to be staged. The connector current sensor of a connector channel shows whether that connector channel is drawing no more than its assigned current limit. The branch current sensor 104 states whether the branch as a whole is still above its limit, whatever the connector channels report, and is the input on which the opening of a contactor at the ordered shedding step 212 depends. A measured branch current above the branch current limit therefore causes a contactor to be opened at the ordered shedding step 212 whatever the connector current sensors report, and no contactor is opened at that step while the measured branch current is below the branch current limit.
The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. Responsive to a command received at the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time through the control-pilot interface of one commanded connector channel, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 is the conductor of that electrical branch and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102, and a reference below to the electrical branch is a reference to the branch supplied by the branch conductor 102. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.

A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. The description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel connected to the branch conductor 102, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.

A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels. The branch current sensor 104 is treated as an independent safety input throughout this description.

An edge controller 106, also referred to herein as a controller, is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108. The isolated local bus 108 carries the assigned current limits, the contactor commands, the pilot reports and the connector current sensor reports between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels.

FIG. 2 shows the first connector channel 120 in more detail. A contactor 122 is connected between the branch conductor 102 of FIG. 1 and a vehicle connector 128. The contactor 122 is controllable by the edge controller 106 and, when open, isolates the vehicle connector 128 from the branch. A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128. A control-pilot interface 126 exchanges control pilot signalling with an electric vehicle 130 that is coupled to the vehicle connector 128. The control-pilot interface 126 signals a current limit to the electric vehicle 130 and reports the presence of a connected vehicle at the vehicle connector 128. The first connector channel 120 is associated with a local connector identifier, which the signed local authorization token names when it authorizes that connector channel.

The current limit signalled through the control-pilot interface 126 is a request addressed to the electric vehicle 130. The electric vehicle 130 governs the current it actually draws. The connector current sensor 124 therefore measures what the connector channel is actually delivering, and the branch current sensor 104 measures what the branch is actually carrying, and neither measurement depends on the cooperation of the electric vehicle 130.

FIG. 3 shows the edge controller 106 and the local fault indicator 116 that it operates. A processing unit 132 executes the allocation and protection functions described below. A session record store 134 holds, for each active connector channel, a charging authorization, a requested current, a minimum sustaining current and an energy-deficit value. The charging authorization records that the session at that connector channel is permitted to draw current. The requested current is the current requested for the session at that connector channel. The minimum sustaining current is the lowest current at which the session is to be maintained. The energy-deficit value is a value stored for the session and used in distributing the remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels.

A network interface 110 receives remote schedules and remote authorizations. A nonvolatile memory 112 holds a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit, as described below. A service input 114 receives commissioning commands from an installer at the installation. A local fault indicator 116 at the installation is coupled to the edge controller 106 and is operated by the processing unit 132 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself. Connections leave the edge controller 106 to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104 as described above with reference to FIG. 1.

FIG. 4 shows the operation of the edge controller 106 over a succession of allocation intervals, and the protective actions that follow when the branch does not respond to the current limits that have been signalled.

At an available current determination step 202, performed at each allocation interval, the edge controller 106 subtracts a measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve from the branch current limit to obtain an available charging current. The measured non-charging branch load is the current on the branch that the edge controller 106 does not command. The configurable safety reserve is a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit. Because the non-charging branch load is measured at each allocation interval rather than assumed, the available charging current follows the spare capacity of the branch.

At a sustaining and deficit assignment step 204, the edge controller 106 first assigns the minimum sustaining current from the available charging current to each active connector channel that can receive the minimum sustaining current, and then distributes a remainder of the available charging current among the active connector channels according to the stored energy-deficit values, thereby obtaining an assigned current limit for each active connector channel. Assigning the minimum sustaining currents first ensures that the capacity of the branch is not divided so finely that every session is left below the current at which it can be sustained.

At a pilot command step 206, the edge controller 106 sends the assigned current limit for each active connector channel through the control-pilot interface of that connector channel, over the isolated local bus 108.

At a connector verification step 208, the edge controller 106 verifies the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel. The verification compares the measured connector current with the assigned current limit for that connector channel.

At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit. So long as the measured branch current is below the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 returns to the available current determination step 202 at the next allocation interval. When the measured branch current is above the branch current limit, the edge controller 106 sends a reduced pilot command, and the verification interval begins when that reduced pilot command has been sent. Meter records for the sessions are appended to a tamper-evident local sequence at the edge controller 106. The sequence is uploaded through the network interface 110 when communication returns, and the accounting for an outage is therefore complete rather than reconstructed.

The service input 114 permits an installer to associate the local connector identifiers with the physical contactors after the field wiring is installed. Responsive to a command received at the service input 114, the edge controller 106 commands one low-energy pilot transition at a time through the control-pilot interface of one commanded connector channel, and it reads the connector current sensors of the connector channels to determine which sensing channel responds. The association between the local connector identifier and the physical contactor is stored only after the responding connector current sensor agrees with the commanded connector channel. Where the responding sensing channel is a different one, or where no sensing channel responds, the association is not stored. Because one connector channel at a time is commanded and the response is confirmed at the sensing channel, a transposition in the field wiring is detected at commissioning rather than being recorded as a consistent but incorrect map. A wiring map error of that kind would otherwise cause the edge controller 106 to apply an assigned current limit to one vehicle connector while verifying the connector current of another, and every subsequent verification at the connector verification step 208 would appear to succeed while the branch was in fact being loaded by a connector channel that no limit was reaching.

The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

All ten findings are fixed and the files are back in sync.

**Critical**
- Claim 5 now ends at "and to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels"; the unsupported isolation boundary is gone from the claim and from ¶7. The disclosure names only "an isolated local bus", so the bus itself is claimed and nothing is asserted about what it isolates from what.
- ¶3 no longer generalizes to "any number of two or more". The paragraph now says the description of the first connector channel applies to each further connector channel connected to the branch conductor 102. The two-block layout stays confined to figures/FIG-1.md and draft/07-drawings.md, which were left unchanged.

**Major**
- ¶19: the safety-reserve sizing rule and the "worst case of an unmeasured load" result are removed; the reserve is now only "a stored margin that keeps the commanded charging current below the branch current limit".
- ¶43: the low-energy pilot transition is now recited by name through the control-pilot interface, with no invented definition of what the transition is sufficient for or does not require.
- ¶9: the local connector identifier is now only what the signed local authorization token names.
- ¶5 and ¶31: the failure, miswiring, scaling-error and "failed low" enumerations are gone. ¶31 keeps only the disclosed division of work between the two measurements and the fact that the branch measurement governs the ordered shedding step 212.
- FIG. 2: the isolated local bus now branches inside the channel to the control-pilot interface block, the contactor outline, and the square outline representing the connector current sensor, so the sensor reports have a route to the controller. ¶7 adds "the connector current sensor reports" to the bus traffic to match.

**Minor**
- "Commissioning mode" is removed from claims 9 and 16 and from ¶43, replaced by "responsive to a command received at the service input". ¶15 now says the service input receives commands from an installer, and ¶43 says a transposition is detected when the association is carried out, so no mode survives anywhere.
- ¶13: the requested current is now "the current requested for the session at that connector channel".
- ¶33: the leakage threshold is now "a stored current value".

Trimming FIG. 2 to add the sensor branch pushed the brief to 2992 characters, over the 2800 limit, so I condensed redundant restatement of the horizontal run and the second "shown schematically" qualifier; it is now 2796 characters with the geometry, contacts, and all seven listed numerals intact. Numeral coverage is unchanged: 27 numerals in the table, each on exactly one sheet across FIG. 1 (8), FIG. 2 (7), FIG. 3 (7), FIG. 4 (8), no sheet over eight.

I did not regenerate rendered sheets: the workspace holds only Markdown figure specifications, and the pipeline renders from them.

input.summary: Fixed all ten review findings. Removed the unsupported isolation boundary from claim 5 and ¶7; removed the "any number of two or more" generalization from ¶3; removed the untraced safety-reserve sizing rule and result, the invented definition of the low-energy pilot transition, the storage-keying function of the local connector identifier, the undisclosed sensor failure modes, the "commissioning mode" operating state in claims 9 and 16 and ¶43, the definition of the stored requested current, and the leakage-threshold selection rule. Gave the connector current sensor a bus branch in FIG. 2 and added connector current sensor reports to the bus traffic in ¶7, then re-trimmed FIG. 2 back under the 2800-character limit.
reasoning: Claim 5 kept the isolated local bus as a structural element but dropped the isolation boundary, because the disclosure names the bus and never says what is isolated from what. The bus is still worth a dependent claim as the disclosed medium coupling the controller to the pilot interfaces and contactors; only the untraceable functional characterization came out.

¶3 was generalizing the channel count solely to reconcile the application text with a two-block drawing. The fix removes the count language entirely rather than restating it, so the description carries only 'each further connector channel' and the drawing's choice of two blocks stays a depiction convention inside the figure brief. draft/07-drawings.md and figures/FIG-1.md were left untouched on purpose: a Brief Description may state what the sheet shows.

The FIG. 2 finding was the one item where the fix adds rather than deletes. The source affirmatively requires that the controller verify the resulting connector current with the corresponding sensor, and the only disclosed controller-to-channel medium is the isolated local bus, so the sensor needed a path. I described it positively as a third branch of the bus reaching the square outline, and dropped the reviewer's 'not crossing one another' phrasing in favour of stating where each branch ends, to avoid a negative linework control.

Adding the third bus branch pushed FIG. 2 to 2992 characters. I recovered the margin by cutting restatement (the horizontal run 'passes through the square outline and continues to the right of it' became 'the run continuing to the right of it') and one duplicated 'shown schematically', not by cutting required geometry or a listed numeral.

¶31 originally argued the point through hypothetical sensor faults. I kept the disclosed asymmetry (the branch sensor governs the shedding step whatever the connector sensors report) and dropped the fault taxonomy, then removed a redundant second 'whatever the connector current sensors report' left by the suggested replacement so the paragraph does not say the same thing twice.

Eliminating 'commissioning mode' from the claims required following the word through the description: ¶15 called the service input a receiver of 'commissioning commands' and ¶43 said a transposition is 'detected at commissioning'. Both now use command and association language, so no reader can infer a disclosed mode state from the specification while the claims recite only a command.

Numeral coverage was re-verified after the edits: 27 numerals in the table, each defined once, each appearing on exactly one sheet, with FIG. 1 and FIG. 4 at the eight-numeral ceiling and no numeral used in the description missing from the table. No claim or abstract carries a numeral.

input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so there is nothing to cite and nothing to distinguish by citation. The Background therefore carries no citation and none was added, since citing a key that is not in the index is prohibited. Claim 1 continues to rest on the disclosed essential relationship rather than on any reference-driven feature: closed-loop per-interval allocation against a branch limit reduced by measured non-charging load and a configurable safety reserve, minimum sustaining current assigned before energy-deficit distribution, pilot delivery verified at the per-connector sensor, and an independent upstream branch measurement that escalates a reduced pilot command into one-at-a-time contactor opening in a stored shedding order after a verification interval. That escalation path, gated on the upstream measurement rather than on the per-connector measurement, is the feature doing the technical work. The Background sets out the problem it solves, that a vehicle may not honour a signalled limit and that a control function assuming its allocation took effect leaves the branch overcurrent device as the only protection, so the argument is in the specification before it is needed. No claim was narrowed or broadened this turn except by removing the two unsupported limitations the review identified.
